properties.description:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Mississippi Sound...
North Mobile Bay...
South Mobile Bay...

* Until 100 PM CDT.

* At 1206 PM CDT, a strong thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located over Fort Gaines, or near Sand Island
Lighthouse, moving north at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Dauphin Island Bridge, Fort Morgan, Heron Bay, East Fowl River
Bridge, Alabama Port, and Portersville Bay.

properties.description:
SMWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island out 20
NM...
Mississippi Sound...

* Until 100 PM CDT.

* At 1152 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 7 nm south of Petit Bois Pass, moving north
at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels and oil rigs...and create suddenly higher waves.
Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Strong winds will be dangerous for boaters or anyone near the water.
Make sure all on board are wearing life jackets. Seek shelter or move
to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

the next 24 to 48 hours.

* Until 230 PM EDT/130 PM CDT/.

* At 1235 PM EDT/1135 AM CDT/, severe thunderstorms capable of

nm south of Panama City Beach to 11 nm east of K Tower, moving
northeast at 70 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage

knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

O Tower, Mexico Beach, S Tower, Empire Mica Wreck, Cape San Blas,
St George Island, K Tower, V Tower, Panama City Beach,
Apalachicola, C Tower, Marker 24 Barge, St. Marks, and Port St.
Joe.

Southwestern Orleans Parish in southeastern Louisiana...

tomorrow evening and continue falling to 10.7 feet Friday
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 25.6
feet on 05/07/2007.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 945 PM CDT.
